title: DRAMA helps Meggitt to investigate Heat Exchange Drainage
summary: Another copy of the MTC case study on Meggitt and MTC validating powder removal from a 70 kg printed AlSi10Mg heat exchanger with sub-millimetre channels on a Solukon machine at NCAM. Up to 99% of internal powder could be drained; the last 1% needs further work.
manufacturing: Two-stage de-powdering on a Solukon SFM-AT800S; drainage experiments.

title: AFRL collaboration yields testing capability for additive manufactured heat exchangers
summary: AFRL opened a test rig for printed fuel-oil coolers under its MAMLS low-cost sustainment programme, run through America Makes. The University of Dayton Research Institute leads the cooler project with DRT Aerospace and GE and had received three printed coolers, tested for pressure drop, flow, inlet and outlet temperatures and particulates. No results are given. The rig is to be open to government and industry after MAMLS.
manufacturing: Printed coolers tested on a new rig, including particulate checks.

title: Surface Heat Exchangers For Aero Engines 2 (SHEFAE 2)
summary: SHEFAE 2 (H2020, 2016-2021, €1.34m) was coordinated by Rolls-Royce with Paulstra and BTU Cottbus-Senftenberg. It aimed to develop lighter integrated heat exchanger systems for turbofans: long, shallow surface air-cooled oil coolers, a fuel-oil heat exchanger with a built-in modulating bypass valve, and mountings that handle thermal and vibration loads, tested on rig and Rolls-Royce demonstrator engines. The fact sheet gives aims only.
thermal: Surface air-cooled oil coolers and a fuel-oil heat exchanger for turbofans.
manufacturing: Manufacturing of high length-to-depth coolers planned; rig and engine tests.

title: Castrol to build immersion cooling development and test facilities
summary: Castrol planned immersion cooling development and test facilities for data centres at its Pangbourne, UK headquarters, part of bp's up to £50m investment there. It will use Submer SmartPod and MicroPod tanks adapted to test new fluids and servers, and develop ways to capture and reuse the heat. Benefits quoted are company claims.
thermal: Immersion cooling of IT hardware and heat reuse.
manufacturing: Test facility with adapted immersion tanks.

title: An investigation of a multi-layered oscillating heat pipe additively manufactured from Ti-6Al-4V powder
publisher: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
summary: A team including ORNL printed a four-layer Ti-6Al-4V oscillating heat pipe (50.8 × 38.1 × 15.75 mm) with an integrated fill port by laser powder bed fusion. It worked at up to 50 W with water, acetone, Novec 7200 and n-pentane in all three orientations tested. Neutron radiography and microscopy showed sintered powder on the channel walls acting as a secondary wick.
thermal: Oscillating heat pipe heat spreader up to 50 W.
manufacturing: Single L-PBF build; neutron radiography and surface metrology.

title: Operational Map And Thermal Performance Of A Thermosyphon Cooling System For Compact Servers
summary: EPFL and Nokia Bell Labs tested a passive two-phase thermosyphon 7 cm tall that fits in a 2U server, using R1234ze(E) and a water secondary loop. It cooled a pseudo-chip at up to 240 W (about 20 W/cm²), and the results were mapped into operating regimes. The abstract gives no further figures.

title: AI server cooling 2026: air vs liquid vs immersion
summary: A UK reseller's guide compares air (25 kW per rack), direct-to-chip (80 kW) and immersion (200 kW+) cooling and gives UK colocation densities of 4-120 kW per rack. Figures are unsourced claims.

title: Validation of Heat Exchangers
summary: DLR's Future Propulsion Test Facility validates aircraft heat exchangers under engine-like conditions, including exhaust heat exchangers that turn liquid into gaseous hydrogen. Cryogenic nitrogen stands in for hydrogen for now. The rig handles hydrogen gas at up to 250 bar and 500 g/s, nitrogen from -196 °C to +150 °C and heated air to 700 °C, for TRL 3-6 tests. No test results are given.
thermal: Exhaust-heated hydrogen evaporators for aircraft engines.

title: Boiling process enhancement on thin zirconium alloy foils
summary: A University of Ljubljana master's thesis laser-textured four surface types on thin zirconium alloy foils and tested pool boiling of water with high-speed infrared thermography. Critical heat flux reached 598-1590 kW/m², 19-217% above the untextured surface, and heat transfer coefficients 34-55 kW/m²K, 30-113% higher. Repeat runs varied little.
manufacturing: Laser texturing; IR thermography in test.
